issues.description: GetLimit mutates shared RateLimit's Stats/FullKey on every request, causing a data race under concurrent traffic
issues.detail: rateLimit is a pointer into the shared config tree. Reassigning rateLimit.Stats and rateLimit.FullKey inside GetLimit without locking is a textbook race — concurrent requests with different runtime values will stomp each other. Stats must be resolved per-call into a local view, not written back into shared descriptor state.

issues.description: Stats counters allocated and discarded on every GetLimit call, leaking into the stats store per request
issues.detail: When the enhanced key differs from FullKey, statsManager.NewStats is effectively called twice — once via the original NewRateLimit and again for enhancedKey — with the first thrown away. On the per-request hot path this registers counters in the store every call. Build the right key once and allocate Stats once.

issues.description: Enhanced-key branch compares against rateLimit.FullKey before it is guaranteed to be set on non-detailed paths
issues.detail: The new code checks `enhancedKey != rateLimit.FullKey`, but FullKey is only assigned in the detailed_metric branch. On non-detailed paths FullKey may be zero-valued or stale from a prior call, so the comparison is undefined against the documented contract. The precondition that FullKey reflects the current stats key is not established before the check.

issues.description: Metric-key construction is duplicated three times inside the lookup loop instead of being abstracted
issues.detail: The matchedViaWildcard, matchedUsingValue, and default-key arms all compute essentially the same thing: append key, optionally with `_` + value. Three near-identical branches should collapse into one helper (e.g. a descriptor-owned `metricSegment(entry, matchKind)` method) so each mode's contract is stated once and the lookup loop stops leaking descriptor internals.

issues.description: Feature duplicates detailed_metric with hand-waved precedence rather than generalizing the existing axis
issues.detail: detailed_metric already supports putting the runtime value into the metric key. value_to_metric adds a parallel mechanism with its own state, its own builder, and an under-specified precedence rule. README does not specify behavior when parent and leaf descriptors disagree, or wildcard interactions. Either extend detailed_metric with a per-level scope or document the cross-level invariant precisely.

issues.description: Positional struct literals for rateLimitDescriptor are fragile against future field additions
issues.detail: Two call sites construct `&rateLimitDescriptor{map{}, rateLimit, nil, descriptorConfig.ValueToMetric}` positionally. Any new field will silently shift argument meanings at every call site with no compile error if types line up. Use named-field initialization so the struct's contract is explicit at construction.

synthesis.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The panel agrees the feature is reasonable but the implementation has serious correctness problems: GetLimit mutates a shared RateLimit pointer from the config tree on every request, which is both a data race and a per-request allocation leak into the stats store. The enhanced-key comparison also reads rateLimit.FullKey on paths where it is not guaranteed to be set. Beyond correctness, the metric-key builder duplicates three near-identical branches inside the lookup loop and largely re-implements detailed_metric with hand-waved precedence. Fix the race by computing Stats per-request without mutating shared state, collapse the key-builder into a descriptor-owned helper, and either extend detailed_metric or document why a parallel axis is required.
